header:
Date: 2027-06-18
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Lynx Head of Payments), Ethan Ross (Platform), Sofia Li (Security), Tom Nguyen (Data Science)
summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling. Customer to share 48h traffic traces and prompt samples. Success metrics discussed: latency p95, cost per 1k requests, and model quality (f1/precision on synthetic evals). Agreement to run Redwood-hosted benchmark followed by Dedicated pilot in VPC if results meet thresholds.
transcript:
00:00:03 - Laura Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - I'm Laura, AE for Redwood Inference, and with me is Daniel, our SE.
00:00:12 - Maya Patel: Hi all, Maya here. we run payments at Lynx, want to see if Redwood can handle our real-time fraud scoring + customer messaging use cases.
00:00:22 - Daniel Ortiz: Great, thanks Maya. can you give us the top-level numbers? qps, size of requests, concurrency?
00:00:30 - Maya Patel: Sure - peak QPS is about 110 requests per second during batch windows, average around 30 qps. Concurrency spikes to ~180 concurrent reqs during batch settlement windows. typical payloads are short: 30 to 80 input tokens, but some enrichment flows send longer context up to ~600 tokens. response sizes vary 20-150 tokens.
00:01:05 - Ethan Ross: to add, many calls are synchronous in-path (payments auth) so latency matters; we target p95 < 300ms for the auth flows. less strict for async messaging.
00:01:18 - Laura Chen: Got it, so we should model both low-latency auth (high qps, small tokens) and long-tail context flows. for the POC we recommend two benchmark profiles: auth profile at 100qps sustained with bursts to 200, 40 token in / 50 token out; and enrichment profile at 10-15 qps with 400-600 input tokens.
00:01:45 - Tom Nguyen: how do you capture tokenization variability? our prompts have user chat history + merchant context so tokens per request vary a lot.
00:01:53 - Daniel Ortiz: we ask for 48 hours of traffic traces ideally with tokenized counts, but if you can't tokenise we can accept raw payloads and run a tokenization pass. we build a distribution: percentiles for input tokens (p50, p90, p99) and same for output.
00:02:15 - Maya Patel: we can export logs, but the logs don't have token counts. Ethan will run a small helper to approximate token counts.
00:02:23 - Ethan Ross: yep, I can run the script. what's the benchmark plan?
00:02:29 - Daniel Ortiz: For the initial bench we'll run Redwood-hosted synthetic load using your traces to re-play traffic. two phases: baseline (hosted API on our shared cluster) to validate perf and then Dedicated pilot on reserved GPUs in your region. metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per second, and cost estimate using Redwood's cost model. we'll also provide KV-cache config suggestions and batching recommendations.
00:03:02 - Maya Patel: important: can we run in our VPC for the Dedicated pilot? security team will require KMS integration and audit logs.
00:03:10 - Sofia Li: yes, SOC2 controls are a requirement. we need SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and key management - ideally HSM/KMS integration.
00:03:20 - Laura Chen: full stop, yes. Redwood Private supports VPC and KMS/HSM integrations. we'll share our security pack (SOC2, ISO attestation, pen test) and a template for the network peering.
00:03:35 - Sofia Li: also data retention - we need to ensure no customer PII is retained in shared hosted environments unless encrypted and contractually allowed.
00:03:43 - Daniel Ortiz: for hosted bench we'll mask PII; for Dedicated pilot we can support customer-managed keys and audit logs. we'll note - the hosted run will be best-effort for traffic fidelity but not for long-term retention.
00:03:57 - Maya Patel: success criteria — what do you propose we measure?
00:04:03 - Daniel Ortiz: propose a few acceptance items: 1) Auth flows p95 latency <= 300ms on Dedicated at target qps; 2) Enrichment flows p95 <= 1.2s; 3) throughput scaling linear-ish with concurrency; 4) cost per 1k requests within agreed threshold - we'll model cost for both scalar and quantized model variants; 5) no regressions in quality on a small eval set (we'll ask you for 200 labeled examples).
00:04:32 - Maya Patel: we want the auth p95 under 250ms if possible; that's our ideal.
00:04:36 - Laura Chen: okay we'll attempt to target 250ms p95 in recommend config, but will state 300ms as realistic SLO depending on model choice.
00:04:45 - Tom Nguyen: about models — do you support our in-house 7B model or only open models?
00:04:51 - Daniel Ortiz: we support a broad model catalog; we can run your in-house or containerized model in Dedicated/private if you provide the artifact and compliance checks. open models and Redwood-verified variants are available on hosted for faster onboarding. note: model quantization and kernel selection affects latency/cost.
00:05:12 - Ethan Ross: how do you simulate real concurrency? replaying traces sometimes doesn't mimic token-level batching.
00:05:20 - Daniel Ortiz: good point. our bench harness replays with arrival timestamps and simulates client-side concurrency; we also run continuous-batching-aware runs to observe effective batch sizes and KV cache hit rates. we can tune the inter-arrival pattern to simulate burstiness.
00:05:38 - Maya Patel: what about cold-starts and KV cache warmup? in auth flows caching helps a lot for repeated contexts.
00:05:45 - Daniel Ortiz: we'll measure cold vs warm throughput and show projected gains with prefix caching. note that long-tail requests (the 600 token ones) will stress memory and kv cache.
00:05:56 - Laura Chen: logistics — to run the hosted benchmark we need: 1) 48h traffic dump or sample, 2) top 10 prompt templates and labeling for 200 eval examples, 3) target qps/concurrency windows you care about, 4) security must-haves for pilot.
00:06:14 - Maya Patel: we'll prepare that. question on timelines: how long for hosted bench and then Dedicated spin up?
00:06:21 - Daniel Ortiz: hosted bench we can run in ~3 working days after we have traces. results + recommendations within 5 business days. Dedicated pilot (VPC peering & reserved GPUs) typically 2-3 weeks depending on procurement and networking.
00:06:34 - Ethan Ross: procurement can be slow - we'll likely need a PO and some legal review.
00:06:38 - Laura Chen: understood - we'll provide a standard SOW template and pricing tiers so you can fast-track procurement.
00:06:45 - Sofia Li: for the security docs, please include SOC2, pen test summary, data flow diagram for hosted vs dedicated.
00:06:52 - Laura Chen: will do.
00:06:57 - Tom Nguyen: on cost modeling - how granular is your cost estimate? we need cost per 1k requests for both peak and average distributions.
00:07:05 - Daniel Ortiz: we provide token-level cost modeling: cost per input token, cost per output token, plus infra amortized cost for Dedicated (GPU hour, memory footprint). we'll produce a few scenarios: optimistic with quantized model and batching, and conservative with FP16/FP32 latencies.
00:07:22 - Maya Patel: what's your recommended model for auth? small LLM? distilled?
00:07:27 - Daniel Ortiz: typically a 3-7B T5-like distilled model works for short auth flows and keeps latency/cost low. but depends on your accuracy needs; we'll evaluate open models and your in-house variants.
00:07:39 - Ethan Ross: what about fallback strategy when Dedicated capacity is saturated? we need graceful degradation.
00:07:44 - Laura Chen: Redwood supports smart routing and fallbacks - route to a cheaper model or to hosted with rate-limit based throttles. we'll show routing policies during the pilot.
00:07:55 - Maya Patel: ok, can you also show a sample dashboard with per-route token cost and p95?
00:07:59 - Daniel Ortiz: yes we'll include sample Console screenshots and a live dashboard for the bench.
00:08:05 - [crosstalk]
00:08:08 - Sofia Li: small nit - do you provide encryption at rest for cache and model weights?
00:08:12 - Daniel Ortiz: yes, for Dedicated we can enable customer-managed keys for storage and KMS for logs.
00:08:18 - Laura Chen: recap: Laura sends pricing + security pack; Daniel shares bench runbook and scripts; Lynx to provide traces and evals. aim to run hosted bench within next week, then decide on Dedicated pilot.
00:08:33 - Maya Patel: sounds good. one more: can you run some latency profiles per-region? we have EU and US traffic.
00:08:40 - Daniel Ortiz: yes we'll run region-specific bench and include latency breakdown per region.
00:08:46 - Tom Nguyen: great. thanks everyone.
00:08:49 - Laura Chen: thanks all - we'll follow up with the artifacts and next steps.
00:08:55 - [meeting ends]
